entries.reason: Selects the rule file and the Conduit plugins.
This converter is not translated by this version of migrate; the wire format of keys would differ.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect until migrate translates the converter.

entries.reason: Kafka Connect trims the list and splits it on commas with surrounding whitespace; written the same way.
The bucket objects are written to.
Kafka Connect rotates a file after flush.size records; Conduit writes one object per batch, so sdk.batch.size bounds the records per object instead.
Conduit has no Avro object format; AvroFormat stores an Avro container file.
entries.fix: Use JsonFormat or ParquetFormat, or keep this connector on Kafka Connect.

entries.reason: The Hive schema generator names the object schema; Conduit has no schema generator.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if a Hive metastore reads the schema, or accept the difference with --accept-gaps.

entries.reason: Conduit has no schema compatibility mode.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if a schema registry or Hive metastore enforces compatibility.

entries.reason: A partitioner whose directory layout Conduit does not reproduce.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if consumers read the partitioned object keys, or use the default partitioner and accept the layout difference.

entries.reason: A time-partitioner path pattern; Conduit has no partitioner path format.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if consumers read the partitioned object keys.

entries.reason: A time-partitioner timestamp source; Conduit has no partitioner timestamp extractor.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if consumers read the partitioned object keys.

entries.reason: The time-partitioner width; Conduit has no partitioner.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if consumers read the partitioned object keys.

entries.reason: A partitioner locale; Conduit has no partitioner.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if consumers read the partitioned object keys.

entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if consumers read the partitioned object keys.

notes.reason: Conduit writes one object per batch as <prefix>/<UnixNano>.<ext>; the Kafka Connect S3 sink names and lays out objects by its partitioner, and its JsonFormat writes the bare record value where Conduit's json format writes one OpenCDC-shaped object per line. Consumers of the exact object keys or line shape break.
notes.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if consumers read the object keys or the bare-value JSON lines, or accept the difference with --accept-gaps.

notes.reason: Object names are not deterministic, so a batch that is retried after a failure or a restart is written again as a new object. A reader can see a record twice, never zero times; Kafka Connect's deterministic naming gives exactly-once object keys.
notes.fix: None needed; consumers should tolerate duplicate objects.

notes.reason: The builtin:kafka source requires servers, and no key of the Kafka Connect config sets it; the pipeline references ${KC_SINK_S3_TRAIN_MOVEMENTS_V00_SOURCE_SERVERS} instead.
notes.fix: Set KC_SINK_S3_TRAIN_MOVEMENTS_V00_SOURCE_SERVERS in the environment (see secrets.env.template), or pass the worker file with --worker if it holds bootstrap.servers.

notes.reason: The builtin:s3 destination requires format, and no key of the Kafka Connect config sets it; the pipeline references ${KC_SINK_S3_TRAIN_MOVEMENTS_V00_DESTINATION_FORMAT} instead.
Neither the connector nor a worker file sets value.converter, so the format Kafka Connect used is unknown.
notes.fix: Pass the worker properties with --worker, or set value.converter on the connector, then re-run.

notes.reason: Kafka Connect does not retry a failed operation by default (errors.retry.timeout=0). Conduit restarts a failed pipeline through pipeline recovery, so a transient failure that stopped the connector may not stop the pipeline.
Kafka Connect's default header converter types header values; Conduit carries headers as metadata strings.
